thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-east-1' error rate spike > 40% and router fallback volume increased 6x. Autopage sent to #eng-oncall and #incidents :rotating_light:

oncall-sre-1: acked, investigating. grabbing dashboards now. pinging runtime team.

runtime-eng-lexi: on it. seeing a big drop in pool.available_replicas for dedicated-east-1 around 22:04 UTC. router started evicting traffic to fallback variants and regions.

infra-eng-omar: can you paste the metric panels? any autoscaler alarms firing?

runtime-eng-lexi: pasted link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ai/routers (shared in thread). autoscaler shows desired=120, actual=0 for several pods in the dedicated pool for ~3m.

oncall-sre-1: that explains blackholing — router thinks there's no capacity and triggers fallback policy cascade. need to confirm if metric is false zero or actual pod drain.

runtime-eng-lexi: running `kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=dedicated-east-1 -o wide` now. logs show pods in CrashLoopBackOff due to config error: autoscaler sidecar failing to mount /etc/pool/manifest (permission denied).

infra-eng-omar: that sidecar mounts changed in yesterday's infra rollout (PR #4586). rolling-restart might help, but need to avoid flapping.

product-ops: any customer impact observed?

customer-success-lina: CS reported 3 customers with increased 5xxs starting ~22:06 UTC. severity: degraded for specific routes hitting dedicated pools. I've opened a support ticket and flagged for status update.

eng-manager-raja: ok, triage -> priority P1. Who can patch the mount quickly? If sidecar can't mount, we should stop the autoscaler from reporting zero to router until we fix.

runtime-eng-lexi: temp mitigation plan: 1) disable router fallback policy for dedicated-east-1 (stop cross-region fallback) 2) scale up pods manually with `kubectl scale` to bypass autoscaler 3) fix sidecar mount in infra PR and roll out. I can do 1 and 2 now.

oncall-sre-1: doing step 1: `POST /api/router/policies/dedicated-east-1/disable_fallback` -> 200 OK. Router logs: "fallback policy disabled for pool dedicated-east-1 by oncall-sre-1". :white_check_mark:

runtime-eng-lexi: running `kubectl -n dedicated scale deployment/dedicated-pool-east-1 --replicas=120` -> command accepted. bridging some capacity now.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager duty event updated: incident assigned to oncall-sre-1 and runtime-eng-lexi.

infra-eng-omar: confirming the mount issue — the infra rollout changed the group id for the pool-config volume, sidecar runs as nonroot and lost access. PR 4592 fixes the volumePermissions init container. preparing hotfix.

product-ops: Lina, please prepare a customer-facing note: short impact, mitigation, ETA for full restore.

customer-success-lina: drafting: "We experienced increased errors for some requests routed to a dedicated capacity pool in us-east. We've applied a mitigation to stop cross-region fallbacks and restored capacity. We're continuing a config fix; next update in 60 minutes."

runtime-eng-lexi: after scaling, error rate dropped to baseline over 3 minutes. Router metrics show fallback traffic -> 0. No further cross-region spills.

oncall-sre-1: monitoring for flapping. leaving fallback disabled until sidecar fix ships.

eng-manager-raja: what's root cause attribution so far? metrics misread or actual capacity loss? We need precise language for postmortem and customers.

runtime-eng-lexi: short answer: combination. infra rollout changed volume permissions for the autoscaler sidecar which caused pod restarts -> actual pod count dropped to zero. router's health-checking/metric consumption relied on `pool.available_replicas` which was produced by the sidecar; zero value triggered fallback cascade. Additionally, router fallback policy had no damping and allowed immediate cross-region cascading which amplified customer impact.

infra-eng-omar: ETA for hotfix? assembling canary now. will push PR 4592 to canary in 10m then promote.

runtime-eng-lexi: temporary routing change worked. next step: add safe-guard in router to ignore sudden zero blips shorter than 2m or consult desired_count before failingover. filing runtime ticket now.

oncall-sre-1: created follow-up tickets: RUNTIME-1243 (router damping + consult desired_count), INFRA-887 (volume permission hotfix), RUNBOOK-56 (how to disable fallback safely).

product-ops: product note posted to status page and customers notified. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2022-dedicated-fallback (placeholder).

customer-success-lina: logged affected customer IDs into the support ticket for follow-up.

eng-manager-raja: thanks team. keep this thread updated. who will own postmortem and blameless writeup?

runtime-eng-lexi: I'll own the postmortem with infra-eng-omar. oncall-sre-1 please add timeline from monitoring.

infra-eng-omar: will follow up with the infra change details and roll history.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Router fallback disabled and pool scaled; error rate returned to normal. Incident severity downgraded to SEV-3.

oncall-sre-1: closing active paging. keeping channel pinned for follow-ups.

runtime-eng-lexi: follow-up notes: - immediate mitigation: disabled fallback policy then scaled pool - root cause: infra rollout changed gid causing sidecar mount failure - contributing factor: router fallback config lacked damping and used single-source metric - customer impact: increased 5xx for targeted routes, 3 customers impacted, no data exfiltration.

eng-manager-raja: assign owners, target timelines: INFRA-887 deploy patch within 2 hours, RUNTIME-1243 change in 1 sprint, RUNBOOK-56 update today.

product-ops: small customer update sent: customers updated with mitigation, ETA for permanent fix 2 hours.

customer-success-lina: will follow up for credits if customers escalate.

runtime-eng-lexi: adding commands used for mitigation for runbook: ```
# disable fallback for pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://router-api.internal/pools/dedicated-east-1/fallback:disable

# scale up pool
kubectl -n dedicated scale deployment/dedicated-pool-east-1 --replicas=120
```

oncall-sre-1: final note: keep fallback disabled until INFRA-887 verified on canary and router damping added. thanks all. :thumbsup:

eng-manager-raja: postmortem owners assigned, please add timeline and blameless analysis in the doc. closing thread when postmortem link is up.
